name: Workflow SDK
title: Qoqi Flow vs Workflow SDK
tagline: Durable without a sandbox, a compiler plugin or a host.
lede: Vercel's Workflow SDK compiles "use workflow" functions into a sandbox that is replayed from an event log: a logical clock, a seeded Math.random, no fetch, no timers, no Node modules. Each run is pinned to the deployment that started it. Qoqi Flow is a whole language that never replays, moves to new code at a stage, and runs anywhere.

cards.title: No sandbox
cards.text: Workflow SDK takes Date, Math.random, fetch, setTimeout and Node modules away from workflow code. A Qoqi flow keeps the whole language; only reaching the world needs a step.

cards.title: Deploy without keeping the old one
cards.text: A Workflow SDK run needs the deployment that started it to stay up for its whole life, or it must be re-run. Qoqi instances move to new code at a stage.

cards.title: Not tied to a platform
cards.text: Built for Vercel, with a Postgres World to self-host. Qoqi Flow is one binary, on any machine, from SQLite to PostgreSQL.

code.title: Wait for an answer, or seven days
code.text: A hook raced against a sleep, and a route of your own to resume it; or one wait match.

code.title: Plain code, because nothing replays
code.text: Workflow SDK swaps the clock and randomness for replayable stand-ins. Qoqi uses the real ones.

faq.q: Is Qoqi Flow ready for production?
faq.a: It is at v0.2.3. The language, the runtime and the daemon work end to end, and they are tested by crashing them on purpose after every write. What it does not have yet is years in production. Start with a flow that matters, not the one that holds the company up.

faq.q: How do Workflow SDK's ideas map?
faq.a: "use workflow": impl Flow. "use step": step fn. createHook and resumeHook: an Inbox field and qoqi send. sleep: wait time.after(...). Promise.race: wait match. FatalError and RetryableError: Result and flow.retry.

faq.q: Do I have to rewrite my services in Qoqi?
faq.a: No. Only the flow is Qoqi. A step that needs your code stays in your service: any server that answers Qoqi's protocol, a signed HTTP POST. qoqi gen writes the typed interfaces for Go, PHP and TypeScript; any other language implements the protocol in a page of code.
Anywhere one binary runs. SQLite on one machine; PostgreSQL or MySQL when several daemons share the work. There is no managed cloud yet.
